title: Jack Teagarden fails to show in Portland
summary: An anecdote of seeing Hallett's band at the Key Theatre in Portland, where Teagarden was drunk and George Troup fell off the stand.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: With this road band, but they didn't last very long. He was trying to make a comeback with all these great names, you know? He had Jack Teagarden with him for awhile, and I saw him -- funny incident -- opened in my home town in the thirties, Jack Teagarden on the trombone, and a very great trombonist called George Troup.

And I went to the Key Theatre to see them open up and I went to see these great names as a kid. At the Key Theatre in Portland, Maine. And I went to see -- oh, who did I just mention? The two trombone players.

But the stage went up, and it was one of the funniest things that ever happened in my life. I went to see Jack Teagarden - he was, we found out later in the Congress Hotel, he was stoned, he was drunk. Didn't make that matinee, and George Troup, the curtain went up and he was supposed to play the Jack Teagarden solo, and he fell off the back of the stand. Now these are the incidents that I thought would break you up a little bit.
Will move or stir you a little bit, anyway.
And Gene Krupa playing the brushes. Let's see, who did I miss in that great band. Well, I named a few.
You named some very good ones.
I think Charlie Spevak played in that band for awhile.
